claims.title: Finite deterministic predictive-equivalence state theorem
claims.scope: one finite hidden-record family and one finite deterministic future-query family whose query is selected after the predictive state is fixed
assumptions: each query has one declared deterministic outcome for every hidden record
one finite predictive state must support every allowed later query
nonclaims: the full hidden record need not be retained when several records have one future-query signature
predictive-state bits are not parent-universe hardware bits

claims.title: Exact single-sink predictive min-cut characterization
claims.scope: one finite directed acyclic integer-capacity network, one source, one sink, and one deterministic future-query family at the sink
assumptions: the source can compute a fixed-length predictive-class label
intermediate nodes may route and recombine exact binary payloads
the sink query is selected after the record-dependent network state is established
nonclaims: the theorem does not optimize latency, total edge use, computation, or robustness
single-sink sufficiency is not promoted into a general multi-sink multicast theorem

claims.title: Weighted deterministic future-query total-variation geometry
claims.scope: a fixed exogenous probability distribution over finite deterministic queries
assumptions: the query distribution is identical under the compared hidden records
the joint law records both the selected query and its deterministic outcome
nonclaims: the identity does not apply unchanged when the query policy depends on the hidden record
the metric is induced by the declared query family rather than by raw record dimension

claims.title: Approximate predictive-packing cut lower bound
claims.scope: a finite family of future laws containing a pairwise greater-than-2-epsilon total-variation packing and a finite capacity cut before the future query
assumptions: one state on the sink side of the cut determines one approximating future law
approximation error is at most epsilon in total variation for every packed record
nonclaims: a packing lower bound is necessary and does not construct an approximate covering or renderer
the exact maximum-clique checker is capped at bounded record families

claims.title: Declared quantum-capacity multiplier for exact predictive labels
claims.scope: exact classical predictive-class labels transmitted over unassisted-qubit or edge-local entanglement-assisted noiseless channels
assumptions: an unassisted transmitted qubit carries at most one exact classical label bit
the assisted model has suitable receiver-side Bell pairs independent of the later hidden record
assisted intermediate nodes may decode and re-encode dense-coded classical payloads
nonclaims: the factor two does not count entanglement creation, distribution, storage, or refresh
the scalar multiplier is not claimed for arbitrary coherent quantum-network tasks

claims.title: Per-sink predictive min-cut necessity
claims.scope: one source and several sinks, each with a declared deterministic future-query family
assumptions: each sink must recover its required future-query signature under the declared capacity model
the theorem is applied separately to every source-sink cut
nonclaims: individually adequate sink cuts do not generally prove simultaneous multicast feasibility
shared bottlenecks and network coding require a separate demand model

claims.title: Coordinate-versus-parity predictive compression
claims.scope: finite m-bit records under either all coordinate queries or a declared family of binary linear parity queries
assumptions: coordinate queries return individual record bits
parity signatures are computed over GF(2)
nonclaims: one parity bit does not reconstruct the full hidden record
the effective predictive dimension changes when the allowed future-query family changes

claims.title: Finite predictive network flow, cut, routing, and packing certificate
claims.scope: bounded finite query families and directed acyclic integer-capacity networks enumerated by the repository
assumptions: maximum predictive packing is searched only below the declared record cap
max flow and route decomposition use the supplied finite graph and integer capacities
nonclaims: a finite certificate is not a proof of unrelated network instances
successful routing is not empirical evidence for a physical simulator
